findings.title: Shipped Darwin 27 arm64 scoping is not asserted against the production table
findings.problem: Every test that exercises architecture scoping swaps in its own copy of the allowlist, so nothing asserts that the production table's new Darwin 27 entry is actually restricted to arm64 and that 27/amd64 is rejected by the shipped map.
evidence: sys_conn_sendmsg_x_qual_darwin_test.go:157-162 replaces qualifiedDarwinKernelMajors with a test-local table before exhausting the kernel/architecture cases
send_conn_sendmsg_x_darwin_test.go:308-312 also replaces the table with a synthetic 'excluded' architecture entry
sys_conn_sendmsg_x_qual_darwin.go:50 is the only place the shipped arch: "arm64" scoping exists, and no test reads it

docs/darwin-batch-compatibility.md:17 requires runtime admission to match native architecture evidence; the original contract states admission table tests exhaust the declared kernel/architecture cases
findings.impact: A future edit that drops or mistypes the arch constraint on the shipped Darwin 27 entry would silently admit Darwin 27 amd64, which has no native qualification, while TestSendmsgXArchitectureAdmission, TestExternalDarwinBatchWriterFallback/architecture and the production-gates command all continue to pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a subtest (or extend TestSendmsgXArchitectureAdmission) that runs the exhaustive declared cases against the real qualifiedDarwinKernelMajors without replacement: 25/arm64 and 25/amd64 admitted, 27/arm64 admitted, 27/amd64 rejected, 26 and 28 rejected. Test-only change; no product edit.

findings.title: Binary README reproduction command points at a stale temporary path
findings.problem: The binary evidence README documents a reproduction path from the original temporary extraction directory, and the extractor writes its outputs next to itself, so the archived instruction is not runnable as written and the safe procedure is documented elsewhere.
evidence: docs/audits/2026-09-22-darwin27-errors/binary/README.md:3 instructs running python3 /tmp/quic-darwin27-binary-research/extract.py, a temporary path that does not exist after checkout
docs/audits/2026-09-22-darwin27-errors/binary/extract.py:4 sets out=pathlib.Path(__file__).parent and lines 40-43 write mapping.json and the three disassembly files beside the script
docs/audits/2026-09-22-darwin27-errors/results.md:54 acknowledges the stale path and prescribes copying the extractor to a scratch directory
findings.impact: A reader following the README's own reproduction command gets a missing-file error, and running the archived extract.py in place would rewrite the frozen mapping and disassembly files (identical bytes on the same kernel, but it still touches frozen evidence and would dirty the checkout). The workaround lives only in results.md.
findings.suggested_fix: State the archived path and the copy-to-scratch step in binary/README.md itself (updating its digest in sha256.json), or have extract.py take an output directory argument so it never writes into the frozen directory.

findings.title: No test checks that the shipped Darwin 27 entry is arm64-only
findings.problem: No test covers the shipped allowlist entry itself. TestSendmsgXArchitectureAdmission and the architecture-excluded fallback test both swap in a synthetic table, so they check the predicate, not the production data. The admission gate test only checks the host's own arm64 case.
evidence: sys_conn_sendmsg_x_qual_darwin_test.go:157-162 replaces qualifiedDarwinKernelMajors with a synthetic table before checking {27, amd64} -> false
send_conn_sendmsg_x_darwin_test.go:308-312 (architecture fallback variant) also swaps in a synthetic table with arch "excluded"
sys_conn_sendmsg_x_qual_darwin_test.go:69-78 checks only the running host's (major, GOARCH), which is arm64
findings.impact: If a later edit drops or changes `arch: "arm64"` on the shipped Darwin 27 entry, amd64 would be admitted without native evidence, against docs/darwin-batch-compatibility.md:17, and every existing test would still pass. The PR's statement that Darwin 27 amd64 remains excluded is currently checked only by reading the code.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small table test against the unmodified production map: sendmsgXQualifiedKernel(27, "amd64") is false, (27, "arm64") is true, and (25, "amd64") and (25, "arm64") are both true. It runs without native execution, so exact-head certification can run it as an ordinary admission unit test.

adjudications.reason: Confirmed by inspection. TestSendmsgXArchitectureAdmission (sys_conn_sendmsg_x_qual_darwin_test.go:157-162) replaces qualifiedDarwinKernelMajors with a synthetic table before checking the (major, arch) cases. The architecture-excluded fallback (send_conn_sendmsg_x_darwin_test.go:308-312) also swaps in a synthetic table. Right now the claim that amd64 stays excluded is backed only by reading the code. The fix is a small test-only table test that needs no native run. It does not change the product and does not invalidate the frozen native evidence. It is low severity because the shipped entry is correct today.
